stories.headline: Paramedic seriously assaulted at Altnagelvin Hospital
stories.body: A Northern Ireland Ambulance Service paramedic with 37 years' service was attacked by a patient for several minutes during a stretcher-to-chair transfer in Derry on Saturday. Police have identified a suspect.
stories.why: She suffered head, neck, face and hand injuries. Violence against crews remains a real risk, even inside hospital.

stories.headline: CQC finds corridor care at Nottingham's QMC
stories.body: A new CQC report rated urgent and emergency care at Queen's Medical Centre as requires improvement, with patients treated in corridors. One 84-year-old waited nearly 40 minutes to be taken off the ambulance.
stories.why: Handover delays at ED keep crews off the road and away from the next 999 call.

stories.headline: North East teams share major-incident lessons
stories.body: NEAS hosted the North East Specialist Capabilities Conference for ambulance, HART, air ambulance and trauma clinicians. Talks included research on 13,000+ trauma patients and a keynote from the first paramedic on scene at 7/7.
stories.why: Worth following if you're interested in a HART or critical care career.

stories.headline: Survivor's campaign funds 10 public defibs
stories.body: A cardiac arrest survivor worked with London Ambulance Service for 18 months to raise over £21,000 for ten public defibrillators in Queen's Park, Kensal Rise, Carlton Vale and Willesden. Nearly 400 residents have been trained in CPR.
stories.why: Bystander CPR and nearby defibs give crews a better chance when they arrive.

stories.headline: Two-day-old baby saved by dad's CPR and EEAST crew
stories.body: A two-day-old girl stopped breathing at home near Ipswich. Her dad started CPR and a crew including a student paramedic arrived within four minutes, joined by a critical care paramedic. She has now been reunited with the team.
stories.why: Early CPR plus a fast response made the difference, and a proud moment for the student on the crew.
